## Senior Data Engineer — Data Platforms & MLOps

I like turning complex, messy data into systems that are reliable and easy to reason about. My career started in renewable energy as a physicist and energy engineer, working on wind resource assessment and solar research — over time my focus shifted toward data, first as a data scientist and eventually as a data engineer, and today I enjoy working where software engineering, data engineering and machine learning intersect.

Recent work spans data lake architecture, production ETL/ELT pipelines, reusable Python infrastructure, and LLM-powered enrichment pipelines that bring structure to unstructured data. Data science has stayed a constant alongside the engineering — multi-model forecasting systems, and more recently applied AI — so I try not to describe myself as only "the platform person." I've worked in startups, scale-ups and established companies, including co-founding an energy-tech company, which taught me that good data solutions need close collaboration with domain experts as much as technical skills.

- **Focus:** data platforms, ETL/ELT pipelines, MLOps, and putting generative AI into production — with a running interest in data science and forecasting
- **Currently:** open to Senior Data Engineer / Data Platform / MLOps roles
- **Experience:** 5+ years in data engineering, 15+ years across data science and renewable energy
- **Stack:** Python, Polars, PySpark, SQL, AWS, dbt, Airflow, Docker, Terraform
- **Languages:** Spanish & Catalan (native), English (professional), French (basic)

### A few highlights along the way

- **Data lake architecture** — a data platform for a multi-country product dataset spanning Spain, France, Italy and Great Britain (S3, Glue, Athena, ECS, Lambda, RDS/PostgreSQL), with entity-level historical tracking of change over time.
- **LLM-powered enrichment** — a dual-provider (OpenAI + Anthropic) batch-processing framework powering 17+ production prompts — ingredient translation, entity matching, claim classification — with prompt-dependency chains, result caching and provider abstraction.
- **Two internal Python libraries** — primary author of the shared data I/O and connectors library at Netquest and the data-lake commons package at Holaluz (I/O, connectors, logging), each versioned, documented and picked up by other teams.
- **Forecasting, a long-running thread** — a multi-model demand/surplus forecasting system (XGBoost, Random Forest, Time Fusion Transformer) for Spain's electricity markets, building on a physics-and-ML forecasting library I first wrote years earlier at Nnergix.
- **Pipeline reliability** — optimizing dbt/Redshift models and moving select PySpark/EMR workloads to Polars in Docker, to make pipelines cheaper to run and easier to debug.
